text:
alex_chen: Heads up team 1 I'm moving to Tokyo for a 3-week client onsite and have an embassy appointment in 5 days. Need: (A) an official confirmation of my recent vaccines + TB clearance they can accept at the consulate, (B) how to submit a claim for the private occupational clinic visit I paid in JPY (receipt attached), and (C) I added my partner to benefits last month but never received an ID 1 can I get an electronic one retroactively?

maria_peopleops: Congrats on the move! :tada: We can do all three. Quick: when did you add the dependent? That affects physical vs e-ID issuance.

alex_chen: Added on 2026-02-08 during OE. Embassy slot is next Thursday, so tight timeline.

sasha_benefits: For the embassy we can issue an "Expedited Coverage & Vaccination Confirmation" PDF today. It shows coverage dates and vaccine entries we have on file. If the consulate needs clinical lab values (e.g., Quantiferon result) you'll need the clinic's signed report.

ben_hr_ops: On the dependent ID: because the change was via open enrollment we can generate a retroactive electronic ID (PDF) now. Tell me partner full name and DOB and I'll trigger it.

alex_chen: Partner: Maya Chen, DOB 1993-07-11. Yes please for the PDF.

maria_peopleops: Ben, can you email the e-ID to alex at alex.ch@redwood.com when ready? Alex, do you have the TB certificate or just the receipt?

alex_chen: I have the clinic receipt (JPY 8,200) and a one-line TB negative stamp in Japanese, but no English translation or detailed lab values.

sasha_benefits: Claims for foreign currency: upload original receipt, an English translation (can be a short typed translation), and the payment proof (bank/cc statement) to the Benefits portal under "Out-of-country medical claims". There's a checkbox to mark foreign currency so we know to convert.

claims_bot: Note: International claims require complete docs. Processing typically 10-15 business days; expedited triage may take 2-3 days after complete upload.

alex_chen: If the clinic adds a short English line like "Occupational TB screen: negative; Hep A booster administered" is that enough?

sasha_benefits: Yes, a concise English description on the clinic letter/receipt is sufficient. CPT/ICD codes optional. If employer/client required the test/vaccine, mark that in the upload notes and we'll treat as occupational/medical.

maria_peopleops: For the embassy letter: Sasha can draft the cover PDF without lab specifics. Many consulates accept that for visa/entry. If they insist on numeric lab results we'll need the clinic-signed report.

ben_hr_ops: E-ID PDF queued. Sending to alex.ch@redwood.com now. If you need a printed copy for the clinic or embassy, that PDF will work as proof.

alex_chen: Thanks! One more: will the vaccine cost be covered as preventive or as medical?

sasha_benefits: If the vaccine/test was required for work/client entry it's covered as occupational medical; if it was elective travel vaccination it's evaluated under preventive rules. We'll confirm once we see the clinic note in the upload.

alex_chen: Uploaded: receipt_tokyo.pdf, tb_stamp_jp.pdf, payment_ss.png. Tagged @sasha_benefits in the portal claim message.

claims_bot: Claim OC-2026-503 created. Expedited triage requested due to embassy timeline. Expect triage in 48-72 hours once docs are verified.

sasha_benefits: I see the upload; marking expedited. Alex, if the clinic can provide a one-line English translation of the TB stamp that speeds things up. If not, paste a quick translation here and we'll accept it.

alex_chen: Will ask clinic now and update. Appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
